info.title: Maverick
info.description: Render Home Assistant dashboards to e-ink displays.

get.description:
The panel catalogue, including the two fields the Add display form
needs to placehold `DisplayConfig.rotation` and `.frame_format`:
`rotation` is `PanelProfile.native_rotation` and `frame_format` is
`PanelProfile.default_format` (`src/maverick/devices/profiles.py`) —
neither was exposed here before the setup UI had a form that resolved
a panel's own value for those two overrides.

Every Lovelace dashboard and its views, for the Dashboard field's picker.

`HomeAssistantClient.list_dashboards` (`src/maverick/ha/client.py`) is
what actually asks Home Assistant; this just gates it behind a working
connection, since a WebSocket call against no client or a broken one
is not something a picker should surface as a 500.

schema.title: Response Ha Dashboards Api Ha Dashboards Get

get.description:
What a form needs to draw itself: the display model plus transport options.

`DisplayConfig.model_json_schema()` carries every field's own
`Field(description=...)` as help text. `TransportConfig` is the one
model that allows extra keys (`extra="allow"`,
`src/maverick/config.py`), so its per-transport options are not in the
schema at all; each transport's own `options_doc`
(`src/maverick/transports/base.py`) is the only description of them
there is, so it is added here under `transports`.

schema.title: Response Display Schema Api Schema Display Get
Response List Displays Api Displays Get

post.description:
Add a display and start rendering it, with no restart.

Every model but `TransportConfig` is `extra="forbid"`
(`src/maverick/config.py`), so a misspelt key such as `panell` fails
here as a **422** naming the field: FastAPI validates the request body
against `DisplayConfig` before this function runs, and the
`ConfigError`s a validator raises are `ValueError`s, which pydantic
turns into the same kind of error as any other bad field.

schema.title: Response Create Display Api Displays Post
Response Get Display Api Displays  Display Id  Get

put.description: Full replacement of an existing display's configuration.

schema.title: Response Replace Display Api Displays  Display Id  Put

delete.description: Stop rendering a display and delete its stored frames from disk.

get.description:
Past render outcomes for this display, newest first.

`Engine.render_history` (`src/maverick/engine.py`) reads from the
bounded, persisted buffer `Engine._notify` appends to on every render —
success, failure, a lint block or an unchanged skip — which is what
lets this answer "what happened" after `DisplayState.last_error` has
already been cleared by a later success.

schema.title: Response Display History Api Displays  Display Id  History Get

post.description:
Pause or resume this display's schedule at runtime.

Distinct from the config-level `enabled` flag, which goes through
`PUT`: this reuses `Application.handle_command`
(`src/maverick/app.py`), the same path the MQTT `schedule_on`/
`schedule_off` commands take, so both publish the same MQTT state.

schema.title: Response Set Schedule Api Displays  Display Id  Schedule Post

post.description:
Put one of a display's pages on the panel and render it.

The page moves before this returns, so the summary it answers with
already names the new one; the render it triggers carries the `page`
trigger and, by default, runs as a background task — a page change
costs a whole render, and a picker that waits out `render.timeout` is
a picker nobody uses. `wait=true` holds the response until the render
finishes, for a caller that wants the outcome.

schema.title: Response Set Page Api Displays  Display Id  Page Post

post.description:
Render a candidate config and hand back the frame. Changes nothing.

`Engine.render_candidate` (`src/maverick/engine.py`) never touches
`states`, `frames` or the display store, and delivers nothing: this is
a dry run for an editor's Preview button, not a save.

schema.title: Response Preview Display Api Displays Preview Post

post.description:
Render one display now.

`wait=false` returns **202** immediately and renders as a background
task, for a caller — the setup UI, behind ingress — that would
otherwise block for the whole render timeout with nothing to show for
it. The default, `wait=true`, keeps the synchronous response
`rest_command` users depend on.

schema.title: Response Render All Api Render Post

get.description: Serve the current frame to a device that fetches on its own schedule.

The frame as a viewable PNG, for the UI and the HA image entity.

Behind the token like everything else it shows, which is why MQTT
discovery stops advertising this URL to the Home Assistant image
entity once a token is set and publishes the bytes over the broker
instead (`src/maverick/ha/discovery.py`): an image entity fetches with
no credentials.

The pre-quantisation capture, downscaled to panel resolution.

Lets the setup UI answer "did the dashboard render wrong, or did the
pipeline do this" without Samba or SSH access to `<data_dir>/frames/`.
Stored by `Engine.render` when `render.keep_screenshot` is set
(`src/maverick/config.py`), independent of the frame a transport
delivers, so it exists for every transport once a display has
rendered — not only for `http_pull`, the one transport that ever
calls `FrameStore.put` (`src/maverick/transports/pull.py`). 404
before the first render, and always when the flag is off.
A ready-to-flash ESPHome config for this display.

A Lovelace dashboard sized for this display's panel.

The gap this fills is the one at the very start: Maverick renders a
dashboard you already have, and the dashboard you already have was
built for a phone. This hands back one built for *this* panel — the
column count and the line budget from its own px and dpi
(`src/maverick/eink/layout.py`), and only cards that survive
quantisation.

The entity list is fetched from Home Assistant so the result names
entities that exist. A failure there is not an error: the generator
falls back to placeholder ids and says so in the file, because a
layout with the wrong entity names is still the right layout, and a
503 here would be the second thing to go wrong for a user whose
credential is what went wrong first.

TRMNL bring-your-own-server handshake.

TRMNL firmware calls this once with its MAC in the ``ID`` header and
expects an API key back. Maverick matches the MAC against a display's
``transport.mac``, so a TRMNL panel needs no extra configuration.

schema.title: Response Auth Status Api Auth Status Get

get.description:
Where Home Assistant sends the browser back.

Home Assistant knows nothing of ``server.api_token``, so this endpoint
cannot sit behind it. The ``state`` nonce is what authenticates the
callback: it was minted by ``/api/auth/start``, which *is* behind the
token, and it is spent on first use.

ColorScheme.title: ColorScheme
ColorScheme.description: The color capability of a panel.

id.title: Id
id.description: Identifier for this display, unique within the file. It becomes a URL path segment and an MQTT topic level.

name.title: Name
name.description: Human-readable name, shown in the setup UI and used for the Home Assistant device. Empty derives one from the id.

panel.title: Panel
panel.description: Panel id from the catalog, as listed by `maverick panels`. It supplies the resolution, color scheme, dpi, rotation, frame format and refresh behavior that the keys below override.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: What to render: a Home Assistant dashboard path such as `/lovelace-eink/kitchen`, or a fully qualified URL. Any scheme counts as absolute, so `file:///...` renders a local page. The single-page shorthand: set this or `pages`, not both.

pages.title: Pages
pages.description: Several dashboards for one panel, rendered one at a time. The page is changed by `POST /api/displays/{id}/page`, by the Home Assistant Page select, or on its own with `rotate`. Empty leaves the display on `dashboard`.

rotate.title: Rotate
rotate.description: Advance to the next page on each scheduled render, once the current page's `dwell` has elapsed. Off leaves the page where it was put.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Render and deliver this display. False keeps it configured but idle.

width.title: Width
width.description: Panel width in pixels. Unset uses the catalog value for `panel`.

height.title: Height
height.description: Panel height in pixels. Unset uses the catalog value for `panel`.

color_scheme.description: Inks to quantize to; see Color schemes. Unset uses the catalog value for `panel`.

dpi.title: Dpi
dpi.description: Pixels per inch, used to turn the theme's millimeter sizes into pixels. Unset uses the catalog value for `panel`.

rotation.title: Rotation
rotation.description: Rotation in degrees applied after fitting, for a panel mounted sideways. Unset uses the panel's native rotation.

frame_format.description: Wire format for the delivered frame; see Frame formats. Unset uses the panel's default format, and failing that a default for the configured transport.

esphome.description: Inputs for the ESPHome configuration `maverick esphome <id>` generates.

DitherMode.title: DitherMode
DitherMode.description: How to map continuous-tone pixels onto the panel's inks.

board.title: Board
board.description: PlatformIO board id written into the generated `esp32:` block.

clk_pin.title: Clk Pin
clk_pin.description: SPI clock pin. The pin defaults are the Waveshare ESP32 driver board pinout, which is what most people actually have; override them per board.

deep_sleep.title: Deep Sleep
deep_sleep.description: Sleep between fetches instead of staying awake, waking on the display's own interval. Essential on battery, and it means the device is unreachable — and so cannot be flashed over the air — between wakes.

buffer_size.title: Buffer Size
buffer_size.description: Bytes reserved for the downloaded frame. Too small and the fetch fails; 0 generates a size from the panel's resolution and color scheme.

verify_ssl.title: Verify Ssl
verify_ssl.description: Whether the generated firmware verifies the server's TLS certificate. Off by default: certificate validation costs an ESP32 memory the frame buffer needs.

node_name.title: Node Name
node_name.description: ESPHome node name. Unset derives one from the display id, as `<id>-panel` with underscores replaced by hyphens.

EsphomeConfig.title: EsphomeConfig
EsphomeConfig.description:
Inputs for the generated ESPHome configuration.

Only needed if you want Maverick to write the device firmware config for
you. Pin defaults match the most common wiring for an ESP32 devkit driving
a Waveshare panel via the vendor's HAT.

dither.description: How continuous tone is mapped onto the panel's inks; see Dither modes.

fit.description: How the screenshot is resized onto the panel; see Fit modes.

serpentine.title: Serpentine
serpentine.description: Alternate the scan direction on each row while diffusing error, which hides directional artefacts. Only the error-diffusion kernels use it: `none` and `ordered` have no error to carry, and `auto` diffuses through Pillow, whose implementation is always left-to-right.

exposure.title: Exposure
exposure.description: Multiplies luminance before quantization. Above 1 lightens.

contrast.title: Contrast
contrast.description: Contrast stretch before quantization. E-ink benefits from a little more than a screen wants.

gamma.title: Gamma
gamma.description: Gamma applied before quantization. Panels are closer to linear than sRGB, so a mild decode keeps midtones from crushing to black.

saturation.title: Saturation
saturation.description: Saturation boost for color panels. Their gamut is small; pushing saturation first means more pixels land on a real ink instead of dithering between two.

sharpen.title: Sharpen
sharpen.description: Unsharp mask radius in pixels. Ink bleeds slightly; a light sharpen restores the edge the panel loses. 0 disables it.

black_level.title: Black Level
black_level.description: Black clip point, 0-255, applied as a level stretch before quantization.

white_level.title: White Level
white_level.description: White clip point, 0-255, applied as a level stretch before quantization.

invert.title: Invert
invert.description: Invert the image before quantization, for a panel wired or mounted to show a negative. Distinct from `pack.invert`, which inverts the packed indices instead.

palette_overrides.title: Palette Overrides
palette_overrides.description: Measured ink values for this panel, keyed by palette name (`black`, `white`, `red`, ...) with `[r, g, b]` values. Despite sitting under `image`, they drive both the quantization palette and the injected stylesheet, so the page is styled with the same inks the frame is quantized to.

blank_ratio.title: Blank Ratio
blank_ratio.description: Fraction of the frame that may be a single ink before `blank_render` calls it blank. That finding is an error, so it also blocks delivery while `block_on_lint_error` is true.

max_ink_coverage.title: Max Ink Coverage
max_ink_coverage.description: Fraction of the frame that may be a non-white ink before `heavy_ink` warns. Dense frames refresh slowly and ghost more.

max_hairline_ratio.title: Max Hairline Ratio
max_hairline_ratio.description: Fraction of inked pixels that may lie on the boundary of the inked area before `hairlines` warns. Text-heavy monochrome frames sit near 1.0 by construction; see the design guide before lowering it.

max_speckle_ratio.title: Max Speckle Ratio
max_speckle_ratio.description: Fraction of the frame that may be isolated salt-and-pepper dither noise before `dither_speckle` warns.

max_spot_coverage.title: Max Spot Coverage
max_spot_coverage.description: Coverage any one spot ink may reach before `spot_ink_overuse.<ink>` warns. Checked for every pigment beyond black, white and the grey ramp.

min_feature_mm.title: Min Feature Mm
min_feature_mm.description: Pixel size in millimeters below which `sub_threshold_pixel` notes that single-pixel detail is under the eye's threshold at reading distance.

msb_first.title: Msb First
msb_first.description: Pack the leftmost pixel of each byte into the most significant bit. False packs it into the least significant bit.

invert.title: Invert
invert.description: Invert the packed indices, so index 0 becomes the last ink. For controllers that clock 1 for white. Distinct from `image.invert`, which inverts the image itself.

plane_order.title: Plane Order
plane_order.description: Ink order for the `planes` frame format, by palette name. Unset packs black first, then the spot colors.

plane_active_low.title: Plane Active Low
plane_active_low.description: Some controllers clock 1 for the *absence* of an ink on the black plane; this inverts each plane to suit them.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: What to render for this page: a Home Assistant dashboard path such as `/lovelace-eink/kitchen`, or a fully qualified URL. Read exactly as `displays[].dashboard` is.

name.title: Name
name.description: Label for this page, shown in the setup UI and offered by the Home Assistant Page select. Empty derives one from the last segment of `dashboard`. Names must be unique within a display, because a page is selected by name.

dwell.title: Dwell
dwell.description: How long this page stays on the panel before `rotate` moves to the next one. Unset advances at every scheduled render; the page never changes faster than the schedule that drives it.

PageConfig.title: PageConfig
PageConfig.description:
One dashboard in a display's rotation.

A display with `pages` renders one of them at a time and moves between them
on command or, with `rotate`, on its own timeline. `dwell` is how long this
page stays up before rotation moves on; unset means it changes at every
scheduled render.

PageSelect.title: PageSelect
PageSelect.description:
Body of `POST /api/displays/{id}/page`: which page to put on the panel.

Three ways to say it, exactly one per request. `index` and `name` are
absolute and `step` is relative — `1` for the next page and `-1` for the
previous, wrapping at either end. They are separate fields rather than one
polymorphic value because an index and a name are not interchangeable: a
page may be called "2" (`Engine.select_page`, `src/maverick/engine.py`).

settle.title: Settle
settle.description: Extra wait after load. Cards that fetch history need a moment.

timeout.title: Timeout
timeout.description: Budget for navigation and for waiting on `wait_for_selector`. Exceeding it fails the render.

supersample.title: Supersample
supersample.description: Render at N times panel resolution then downsample. 2 gives markedly better text on low-dpi panels; it costs memory and time.

viewport_width.title: Viewport Width
viewport_width.description: Browser viewport width, if it should differ from the panel's logical size. Used only when `viewport_height` is set as well.

viewport_height.title: Viewport Height
viewport_height.description: Browser viewport height, if it should differ from the panel's logical size. Used only when `viewport_width` is set as well.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.description: Zoom the page before capture; Home Assistant's own layout breakpoints respond to it. With the theme enabled it multiplies the dpi-derived zoom rather than fighting it.

wait_for_selector.title: Wait For Selector
wait_for_selector.description: CSS selector to wait for before capturing. Unset waits for `home-assistant`, which is present on every Home Assistant page.

crop_to_selector.title: Crop To Selector
crop_to_selector.description: CSS selector to capture instead of the whole page. A selector that matches nothing fails the render rather than capturing the page.

wait_for_images.title: Wait For Images
wait_for_images.description: Wait until every `` has decoded. Weather icons are usually the slowest thing on the page.

debug_artifacts.title: Debug Artifacts
debug_artifacts.description: Keep the pre-quantization screenshot next to the frame preview and the lint report, under `<data_dir>/debug/<id>/`.

keep_screenshot.title: Keep Screenshot
keep_screenshot.description: Keep the pre-quantisation screenshot, downscaled to the panel's resolution, so the setup UI can show the source render next to the quantised frame — the question `debug_artifacts` otherwise needs Samba or SSH to answer. Stored in memory and under `<data_dir>/frames/<id>.screenshot.png`, one PNG at panel resolution per display; turn it off to save that memory.

RenderConfig.title: RenderConfig
RenderConfig.description: How the browser should capture the dashboard.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Include this display in the scheduler. False leaves it renderable on demand only; a Home Assistant switch can also pause it at runtime without editing this file.

every.title: Every
every.description: Render on a fixed interval. Mutually exclusive with `cron`.

cron.title: Cron
cron.description: Render on a five-field crontab expression, in the server's local time zone. Mutually exclusive with `every`.

quiet_hours.title: Quiet Hours
quiet_hours.description: Skip scheduled and state-triggered renders in this window. Format "23:00-06:30"; a window may wrap midnight. Renders asked for by hand, by the API or at startup ignore it.

on_change.title: On Change
on_change.description: Entity ids to watch: a state change on any of them re-renders the display. It needs a Home Assistant connection, and attribute-only updates are ignored.

debounce.title: Debounce
debounce.description: Ignore `on_change` bursts closer together than this.

full_refresh_every.title: Full Refresh Every
full_refresh_every.description: Force a flashing full refresh every N frames to clear ghosting. 0 uses the panel profile's recommendation.

skip_unchanged.title: Skip Unchanged
skip_unchanged.description: Skip delivery when the frame is byte-identical to the last one.

render_on_start.title: Render On Start
render_on_start.description: Render once at startup rather than waiting out the first interval.

ScheduleConfig.title: ScheduleConfig
ScheduleConfig.description:
When to re-render.

``every`` and ``cron`` are mutually exclusive. ``on_change`` subscribes to
Home Assistant's state stream, which is how a render follows the data
instead of a clock.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Inject the generated e-ink stylesheet. False leaves Home Assistant's own styling in place and applies `extra_css` alone.

body_mm.title: Body Mm
body_mm.description: Height of body text in millimeters on the panel, converted to pixels using the panel's dpi. It is a physical size, not a browser font size.

scale_ratio.title: Scale Ratio
scale_ratio.description: Ratio of the modular type scale: each step up multiplies by this.

min_font_weight.title: Min Font Weight
min_font_weight.description: Minimum font weight. 400 is the floor at which stems survive 1-bit output.

strong_font_weight.title: Strong Font Weight
strong_font_weight.description: Weight used for headings and numeric readouts.

rule_mm.title: Rule Mm
rule_mm.description: Border width in millimeters — hairlines disappear below roughly 0.2 mm.

radius_mm.title: Radius Mm
radius_mm.description: Card corner radius in millimeters. Sharp corners dither more cleanly.

font_stack.title: Font Stack
font_stack.description: CSS font stack for the page. Unset uses the built-in e-ink stack, which prefers faces whose stems survive quantization.

hide_chrome.title: Hide Chrome
hide_chrome.description: Hide the Home Assistant toolbar, sidebar and other frontend chrome.

use_spot_colour.title: Use Spot Colour
use_spot_colour.description: Let the panel's spot ink carry alerts and state highlights. The ink is used as a text color where it is legible against the panel's white, and as a highlight fill under the foreground ink where it is not — yellow is 1.3:1 as text and 6.9:1 under black. It has no effect on a panel without a spot ink.

letter_spacing_em.title: Letter Spacing Em
letter_spacing_em.description: Letter spacing in em. Unset derives it from the panel's dpi: 0.012 below 150 dpi, where adjacent stems smear together, and 0 above.

extra_css.title: Extra Css
extra_css.description: CSS appended verbatim, last, so it can override anything the theme generates. It is applied even when `enabled` is false.

css_file.title: Css File
css_file.description: Path to a CSS file merged after `extra_css`. A path that does not exist fails the render rather than being skipped.

ThemeConfig.title: ThemeConfig
ThemeConfig.description: Overrides for the injected e-ink stylesheet.

type.title: Type
type.description: Registry name of the transport that delivers the frame. Unset uses the panel's own `default_transport` from the catalogue — a BLE shelf label delivers over `opendisplay` and a Waveshare module over `http_pull` without being told. Every other key in this section is that transport's own option; see Transport options.

TransportConfig.title: TransportConfig
TransportConfig.description:
Where the finished frame goes.

Extra keys are permitted and handed to the transport, because each one has
its own options and forbidding them would mean restating every field here.
